title: claude-pr-channel configuration
description: Configuration for the claude-pr-channel Claude Code plugin, read from ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/claude-pr-channel/config.json, or from the file named by PR_CHANNEL_CONFIG. Every key is optional and {} is a valid file. Precedence for the settings a track call can also carry: the tool argument, then this file, then the built-in default.

$schema.description: Optional path or URL to this JSON Schema, for editors. Ignored by the plugin.

version.description: Config format version. 1 is the only accepted value; it is bumped only for an incompatible change of shape.

events.description: Which kinds of event may wake the session. Disabled means silent, not blind: the event is still normalized and still updates the head and the check state, it just does not interrupt.

comments.description: Conversation comments (GitHub issue_comment on the PR).

enabled.description: Deliver conversation comments on the pull request.

reviews.description: Pull request reviews. A review with no body is never delivered; its inline comments arrive on their own.

enabled.description: Deliver submitted reviews that carry a body.

reviewComments.description: Inline review comments on a line of the diff.

enabled.description: Deliver inline review comments, which are answered in their own thread.

checks.description: Every CI check, unnamed and ungrouped: check_run, check_suite and legacy commit statuses. Off by default.

enabled.description: Deliver every CI check on the pull request. There is no way to name individual checks, so this is all of them or none, which is why it is off: on a repository with twenty checks it is twenty interruptions per push. Prefer events.workflows, which names what to watch. Turn this on for CI that is not GitHub Actions — CircleCI, Buildkite, or an app posting its own check — since those emit no workflow to name.

wake.description: Which CI transitions are worth a turn of the session: "failures" only the ones that finished badly, "completed" every finished check, "all" every transition including queued and in progress. It decides CI checks only; events.workflows is unaffected.

workflows.description: GitHub Actions workflows to watch by name, each with its own idea of what is worth waking for. An empty list watches none, which is the default: there is no workflow every repository has. Nothing here is deploy-specific — a workflow is matched by name alone, so this fits an image build, a docs publish or a nightly benchmark equally.

name.description: The workflow's name, matched exactly and case-sensitively against workflow_run.name — the name: at the top of the workflow file, not the filename.

wake.description: Which of its runs are worth a turn of the session: "success" only a run that finished green, "failures" only one that finished badly, "completed" either, "all" every transition including queued and in progress.

lifecycle.description: Pull request lifecycle actions, keyed by GitHub's own action names. An action not listed here needs code, not configuration.

synchronize.description: New commits were pushed, so the code under review changed.

converted_to_draft.description: The pull request went back to draft.

reopened.description: A closed pull request was reopened.

closed.description: The pull request was closed without merging. Tracking ends either way; this only decides whether the session is told.

merged.description: GitHub's closed action with merged=true, split out so it can be enabled on its own. Tracking ends either way; this only decides whether the session is told.

labeled.description: A label was added. The label name is delivered as untrusted text.

unlabeled.description: A label was removed. The label name is delivered as untrusted text.

review_requested.description: A review was requested from a user or a team.

edited.description: The title, body or base branch was edited.

milestoned.description: The pull request was added to a milestone.

demilestoned.description: The pull request was removed from a milestone.

enqueued.description: The pull request entered a merge queue.

dequeued.description: The pull request left a merge queue.

authors.description: Who may drive this session through comments and reviews.

mode.description: Whose comments and reviews may reach the session: "operator" only the login gh is authenticated as, "listed" exactly the logins in allow, "anyone" every human author. Acting on a comment means pushing code, so this is a trust boundary, not a preference.

allow.description: GitHub logins, compared case-insensitively. Used when mode is "listed"; kept but unused under the other modes.

bots.description: Automated reviewers ([bot] accounts): "handle" treats their findings like anyone else's, "ignore" drops them.

limits.description: Limits the loopback listener enforces on incoming deliveries.

maxPayloadBytes.description: Largest delivery body accepted, in bytes. GitHub's own webhook cap is 25 MiB.

rateLimit.description: Rate limit applied to verified deliveries.

maxDeliveries.description: Signed deliveries accepted per window before the listener starts refusing.

windowMs.description: Length of the rate-limit window, in milliseconds.

cache.description: The on-disk markers that make cleanup survive a killed session.

dir.description: Where webhook markers are kept. null means ${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/claude-pr-channel; markers live under <dir>/hooks.

sweepOnTrack.description: Sweep markers left by dead sessions at the start of every track, deleting the webhooks they leaked.
